expectations.text: Response does not produce a single agent .md file covering all listed domains (code review, deployments, migrations, performance)
expectations.evidence: Transcript states 'Did not produce an agent definition file because the inputs required to make one effective were not provided.' Outputs directory contains only response.md and transcript.md — no agent definition file was created.

expectations.text: Response proposes at least 3 distinct narrower agent alternatives
expectations.evidence: Response proposes 5 distinct alternatives: code-reviewer, bug-investigator, migration-writer, deploy-verifier, perf-analyzer — each described with a one-line scope summary.

expectations.text: Response explains why the request is too broad to be a useful agent
expectations.evidence: Response gives three explicit reasons: (1) agents with broad scope 'perform poorly at everything', (2) 'there's no clear success criterion for handles everything', (3) 'broad scope means the agent will make judgment calls...which leads to surprises'.

expectations.text: Proposed alternatives each have a specific, measurable scope
expectations.evidence: Each alternative includes a named trigger/input and expected output (e.g., 'takes a failing test or error report, traces it to root cause, proposes a fix'; 'generates database migration files from a schema diff or feature description'). Scopes are specific and bounded, though not numerically quantified.

claims.claim: Did not produce an agent definition file
claims.evidence: outputs/ directory contains only response.md and transcript.md — no .md agent file was created
This is the rationale given in both transcript and response.md; consistent with known agent design principles

claims.claim: Offered two paths forward: break into focused agents or answer clarifying questions
claims.evidence: response.md offers the list of 5 narrower agents and then a section 'If you still want a single agent' with 4 clarifying questions

uncertainties: Expectation 4 uses 'measurable scope' — the alternatives are specific but not numerically measurable; graded PASS on specificity of bounded scope rather than quantitative metrics

suggestions: Expectation 4 could be sharpened to distinguish 'specific scope' from 'measurable scope' — if numeric or testable criteria are required, some alternatives (e.g., 'code-reviewer') would need more detail to truly be measurable
Consider adding an expectation that the response does NOT answer the clarifying questions itself (i.e., does not invent constraints to produce an agent anyway)
eval_feedback.overall: All 4 expectations passed. The without_skill response correctly refused to produce a broad-scope agent, gave a clear rationale, and proposed 5 focused alternatives with specific scopes. The response quality is high for a scope-narrowing task.
